answer: What if each ballot had to prove a body stands behind it? World's Orb has verified nearly 18 million irises, each yielding one zero-knowledge nullifier — a signal no two people share. A ballot enrolls its nullifier, and any second ballot carrying a duplicate dies on the spot. A farm trying to forge 10,000 ballots needs 10,000 irises: each Orb scan takes ten minutes, so 10,000 scans burn 1,667 hours, each fake forfeits a $25 bond, $250,000 burned, and 10,000 stand-ins at $50 a head cost $500,000. Like umber, one earth gives one shade — a copied iris is a dead ballot and a $750,000 lesson.
